care_continuity: CTE, CME, and creche construction monitoring continued at CME, ISTM Nyankunde, HGR Rwampara, and Elykia.
Nutrition follow-up continued in all CTEs.
Five health facilities were evaluated in Nizi and recovery plans were prepared for evaluated facilities.
community_engagement: Nord-Kivu sensitized 11,853 people, engaged 77 community actors, used 18 radio channels for shows/spots, and logged 11 community alerts.
Sud-Kivu advocacy involved 45 leaders in Katana, a CREC meeting in Miti-Murhesa, and briefing of 10 CREC members.
Ituri evaluated Mongbwalu activities and engaged Shari authorities around funeral-prayer risk near the Balidja morgue in Rwampara.
context: The affected Ituri area borders Uganda and South Sudan and has chronic humanitarian constraints, cross-border movement, artisanal mining, armed-group activity, and more than one million internally displaced people.
The outbreak origin remains described around Mongbwalu in Djugu territory, about 70 km from Bunia.
The outbreak was officially declared on 2026-05-15.
coordination: Evaluation and coordination missions continued in Beni and Butembo.
CHU Cinquantenaire Kinshasa agent briefing was underway.
A SGI, partner, and national-expert session in Rwampara focused on surveillance, contact listing, and follow-up.
National and provincial SGI training closed during the reporting cycle.
highlights: 17 new confirmed cases including 5 confirmed deaths were reported for 2026-06-11.
New confirmed cases were in Bunia (6), Rwampara (5), Mongbwalu (4), and Nizi (2).
COUSP and national incident-management teams supervised CTE Butembo and Katwa.
INSP leadership and a COUSP/WHO multidisciplinary team arrived in Butembo.
CTE Rwampara received a cardiac monitor and pulse oximeter.
infection_prevention_control: Ituri continued training and briefings in Komanda, Nyankunde, and Bambu, and decontaminated two health facilities and two households.

Nord-Kivu evaluated four health facilities, decontaminated two, briefed 46 of 56 providers across 14 of 17 facilities, evaluated exposure risk for 15 of 36 providers, and supported 26 facilities in Goma, Karisimbi, and Nyiragongo.
Sud-Kivu decontaminated 12 households and 9 toilets, supported safe sampling work, briefed hygienists at CS Kahungu, and supported Kahungu and Kalagane.
laboratory: Ituri reported 35 samples collected and analyzed, with 17 positives and 48.6% positivity.
Nord-Kivu reported 172 samples pending with a delay greater than five days.
logistics_security: Medicines and IPC supplies were delivered to Rwampara, and CTE/CME Bunia materials were delivered.
Bunia and Rwampara were relatively calm, while armed-group activity in Djugu, Irumu, and Mambasa continued to limit humanitarian access.
psea: Ituri PSEA sessions included PAM-supported participants, FHI360 participants, and a leader session with code-of-conduct signatures recorded.
Nord-Kivu second-wave sensitization in Goma and Beni reached community relays and leaders, with code-of-conduct signatures recorded.
Sud-Kivu briefed response actors and providers at CS Kabushwa and teachers in Miti-Murhesa and Lwiro.
publication_context: INSP SitRep 28 reports data through 2026-06-11 and was published 2026-06-12.
The outbreak remains reported across 3 provinces and 29 health zones; no newly touched health zone is reported for this cycle.
Ituri remains the epicenter with 646 of 689 DRC confirmed cases (93.8%).
Nord-Kivu is harmonized to 40 confirmed cases from the prior 44-count state; the SitRep footnote attributes this to national SGI data harmonization.
Sud-Kivu has reported no new confirmed case since 2026-05-26.
redactions: Page 11 contact details are intentionally not promoted into public evidence text.
surveillance: 419 alerts were reported and 377 were investigated, producing a 90.0% investigation rate.
168 suspected cases of the day were validated, including 64 deaths.
234 new contacts were listed in Lita (115), Nizi (101), Bambu (14), and Kambala (4).
Rwampara and Bunia contact follow-up data were unavailable despite representing 55.6% of Ituri contacts, lowering the global follow-up rate to 28.4%.

challenges.finding: Reluctance to post-mortem swabbing can delay confirmation and underestimate mortality.
challenges.response: Strengthen community engagement and religious-leader involvement.

challenges.finding: Normalized CTE capacity remains insufficient despite Rwampara opening.
challenges.response: Accelerate planned CTE construction.

challenges.finding: MEG supplies remain insufficient in targeted HGRs.
challenges.response: Continue advocacy and resource mobilization.

challenges.finding: IPC materials are insufficient in Nord-Kivu, increasing nosocomial risk.
challenges.response: Urgent supply reinforcement.

challenges.finding: Alert reporting remains weak across the three affected provinces.
challenges.response: Strengthen community surveillance.

challenges.finding: Insufficient resources across pillars slow operations; the SitRep cites a USD 21.5M gap.
challenges.response: Resource mobilization.

Continuity of care reports 109 confirmed people-deprived-of-liberty (PPL) cumulative in Ituri, of whom 34 died (31.2%) and 46 recovered. 774 hot meals were served (150 to confirmed cases, 127 to suspected cases, 446 to PPLs, 52 to caregivers).
highlights: 26 new confirmed cases including 9 community deaths were reported for 2026-07-03, in Ituri (21 including 6 deaths) and Nord-Kivu (5 including 3 deaths). In total 19 confirmed deaths were recorded over the day: the 9 community deaths plus 10 deaths among previously confirmed CTE/CT patients (8 Ituri, 2 Nord-Kivu Katwa), bringing confirmed deaths to 492.
The 26 new cases came from Rwampara (11), Bunia (5), Mongbwalu (3) and Mangala (2) in Ituri and from Butembo (2), Musienene (1), Masereka (1) and Beni (1) in Nord-Kivu.

Nord-Kivu cumulative counts were re-actualized this cycle: alongside 5 new confirmations the province table shows a within-province reclassification (Goma 2->1, Kyondo 3->4), a net +5 consistent with DHIS2 cleaning/harmonization.

10 patients recovered (9 Ituri, 1 Nord-Kivu Katwa), bringing DRC cumulative recoveries to 239. Mongbwalu carries a 50.4% case-fatality (139 deaths for 276 cases); Nord-Kivu remains the highest-lethality province at 58.0%, led by Katwa (72.5%), Oicha (66.7%) and Beni (58.6%).

Nord-Kivu collected and analyzed 93 samples with 5 positive (5.4%). Sud-Kivu collected 5 samples still under analysis. New diagnostic labs are being installed at Komanda, Nizi, Mambasa and Nia-Nia (Ituri).
publication_context: INSP SitRep 50 reports through 2026-07-03 and was published on the INSP WordPress site (post 25088; embedded PDF media 25089; WP publish 2026-07-04T19:32:31Z). SitRep50 supersedes SitRep49 directly (a single report-day advance); the cumulative rose by 26 confirmed and 19 deaths over 2026-07-03.
The outbreak is reported across 3 provinces and 36 of 104 health zones; no newly affected zone was reported this SitRep.
Ituri remains the epicenter with 1387 of 1528 DRC confirmed cases (90.7%) and 411 deaths (CFR 29.6%).
Nord-Kivu holds the highest provincial confirmed-case fatality ratio at 58.0%, led by Katwa (72.5%), Oicha (66.7%) and Beni (58.6%); 100% lethality observed in low-count Vuhovi.
redactions: Page contact details and operational names, if present outside table facts, are intentionally not promoted into public evidence text.
surveillance: 1131 alerts of the day were reported (60 J-1 + 1071 new) and 902 investigated (Tableau 3), a 79.7% investigation rate; Ituri 34.2% (119/348), Nord-Kivu 100.0% (768/768), Sud-Kivu 100.0% (15/15).
185 suspected cases of the day were identified, including 67 deceased validated alerts.

9971 contacts were under follow-up and 8126 were seen, producing 81.5% follow-up coverage; Ituri 82.3%, Nord-Kivu 78.9%. The rate is computed only for reporting ZS (completeness 90%); Bunia, Aungba and Nia-Nia (Ituri) had no contact data at consolidation.

329 new contacts were listed (132 across 4 Ituri health zones and 197 across 3 Nord-Kivu health zones); 501 contacts completed 21-day follow-up (384 in Ituri, 117 in Nord-Kivu); 44 contacts became suspects (all in Ituri).

A dead body arriving from Uganda toward the DRC (Beni) was intercepted at the Kasindi PoE; 3 dead bodies were intercepted at PoE/PoC overall. A security incident (vandalism) was reported at PoC Irumu Centre.

Community-death analysis (SitRep50): the majority of recorded deaths are community deaths, concentrated in Mongbwalu, Bunia and Katwa, with late presentation to health structures raising the risk of secondary household transmission. These sub-cohort figures are qualitative context and are not used as denominators for the 492 confirmed-death total.

challenges.finding: Community reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and resistance delay confirmation, underestimate cases, and disrupt key activities.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, and reinforce team security.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE capacity with Nord-Kivu saturation cited at 138.8% in the challenge table; the banner reports national isolation occupancy 89.4% (628 patients), raising nosocomial-transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction/expansion and deploy additional temporary isolation structures.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up performance reached 81.5% (challenge table cites 81.3%) versus the 95% target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy, and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Weak alert reporting in some affected health zones risks undetected, silent transmission.
challenges.response: Reinforce community-based surveillance and rapid alert investigation.

challenges.finding: Seventeen Ituri confirmed cases remain not yet ventilated by health zone, leaving gaps in transmission-chain reconstruction.
challenges.response: Conduct data reconciliation, prune duplicates, and reclassify/localize with active field verification.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited training raise nosocomial-infection risk; the challenge table reports 96 health-worker infections and 19 deaths (CFR 19.7%).
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: A backlog of un-analyzed samples in Nord-Kivu and late diagnosis persist amid a 54.2% provincial CFR (challenge table).
challenges.response: Deploy a laboratory catch-up plan and reinforce diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and isolation structures (a gap of about 20 centers) delay transfer and isolation and raise transmission risk.
challenges.response: Urgent deployment of logistics and additional infrastructure.

challenges.finding: Insufficient coordination and weak use of COUSP frameworks cause operational inefficiency and delayed decisions.
challenges.response: Reinforce coordination mechanisms at all levels and operationalize provincial COUSP.

challenges.finding: A financial-resource gap of about USD 20 million limits implementation across all response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and partner advocacy.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations and access to high-risk zones.
challenges.response: Strengthen security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Compromised continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services raises indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effectively implement free care and reinforce continuity of essential health services (CEHS).

challenges.finding: High population mobility raises the risk of rapid geographic expansion; this cycle a dead body arriving from Uganda toward the DRC was intercepted at the Kasindi PoE (Beni, Nord-Kivu), and the Wamba/Haut-Uele imported cases stay counted within Nia-Nia (Ituri).
challenges.response: Reinforce PoE/PoC surveillance and cross-border/inter-provincial coordination.

The 1,528 confirmed total is marked re-actualized and subject to change after DHIS2 cleaning/reclassification/harmonization; SitRep50 supersedes SitRep49 directly (a single report-day advance), so treat the +26 confirmed and +19 confirmed deaths vs SitRep49 as an official one-day delta for 2026-07-03.

Nord-Kivu cumulative counts were re-actualized: alongside 5 new confirmations the province table carries a within-province reclassification (Goma 2->1, Kyondo 3->4), a net +5 change consistent with data cleaning rather than 5 additional field notifications plus a lost case.
SitRep50 carries an explicit Ituri residual of 17 confirmed cases in zones not yet identified; these counts are public but not mappable to named health zones.
No new affected health zone was reported this cycle; the affected-zone count remains 36 of 104 (Ituri 24/36). No new map geometry was required.
The banner case-fatality is 32.2% (492/1528).

The isolation census (628 at 89.4% occupancy) is re-reported only in the SitRep50 banner and is unchanged from SitRep49's end-of-day census; SitRep50 published NO fresh patient-movement (CTE/CT/CI) table, so the confirmed/suspected split (215 confirmed / 413 suspected) is carried from SitRep49's last published Tableau 6 split and still reconciles to the 628 census (215 + 413 = 628). It is a carried/reconciled estimate, not a freshly reported table. Nord-Kivu isolation occupancy is 136% (138.8% saturation cited in the challenge table).
Daily suspected cases (185) and the 67 deceased validated alerts are current-cycle validated alert outputs, not cumulative suspected stock or cumulative confirmed deaths.

Uganda anchor remains 20 cumulative confirmed cases (2 deaths, 11 recoveries) per the Uganda MoH EVD daily dashboard (last reviewed 2026-06-21); WHO AFRO Uganda External SitRep 07 (data as of 2026-06-28) independently reports no new confirmed Uganda cases over the past week. Carried forward this cycle as INSP reports DRC only, so country-scope is 1548 confirmed / 494 deaths / 250 recovered.

Sud-Kivu has recorded no new confirmed case since 2026-05-26, suggesting no recent transmission; it remains at 3 confirmed / 1 death across Miti-Murhesa, and its contacts remain exited from follow-up.
Several low-denominator zones report 100% case-fatality this cycle (Drodro 3/3, Kambala 2/2, Vuhovi 1/1, Lolwa 1/1); these are unstable small-number ratios.

The challenge table cites 96 health-worker infections with 19 deaths (CFR 19.7%), a Nord-Kivu CTE saturation of 138.8%, a Nord-Kivu laboratory backlog amid a 54.2% provincial CFR, an isolation-structure gap of about 20 centers, and a financing gap of about USD 20 million.

A community-death sub-analysis in SitRep50 (majority of deaths occurring in the community, concentrated in Mongbwalu, Bunia and Katwa; late presentation to care) is internally inconsistent with the cumulative confirmed-death total and is treated as qualitative context only, never as a denominator.

External response milestones reported outside the INSP SitRep are tracked as separate context in the LOVS narrative/synthesis, not in the INSP denominators: the WHO Emergency Use Listing of the first BDBV molecular RT-PCR diagnostic (2026-07-02) supports the SitRep-noted decentralization of diagnostic capacity (new labs at Komanda, Nizi, Mambasa, Nia-Nia); and the response financing picture (INSP-cited ~USD 20 million pillar-implementation gap; separately, an Africa CDC response requirement of ~USD 1.4 billion with pledges only ~13% released, a White House/OMB supplemental request of ~USD 1.4 billion still before Congress, and OCHA/UNDP macro-humanitarian and socioeconomic context) is recorded as distinct facets and not collapsed into a single figure.

highlights: 63 new confirmed cases including 8 community deaths were reported for 2026-07-05, in Ituri (60 including 15 deaths) and Nord-Kivu (3). Confirmed deaths rose to 521 (+15 vs SitRep51).

The 63 new cases came from Bunia (14), Mongbwalu (10), Nia-Nia (8), Bambu (7), Mangala (7), Nizi (6), Rwampara (5), Fataki (1), Rimba (1) and Nyankunde (1) in Ituri and Musienene (2) and Masereka (1) in Nord-Kivu.
No new affected health zone was reported on 2026-07-05; affected zones remain 36/104. Sud-Kivu has recorded no confirmed case since 2026-05-26.
Response activities were stopped in the Bunia health zone by providers (strike).
Nord-Kivu remains the highest-lethality province at 56.3%, led by Katwa (73.1%), Oicha (66.7%) and Beni (58.6%); Mongbwalu carries 51.7% (149 deaths for 288 cases).

challenges.finding: Community reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and resistance delay confirmation, underestimate cases, and disrupt key activities.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, and reinforce team security.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE capacity with Nord-Kivu saturation cited at 138.8% in the challenge table; the banner reports national isolation occupancy 89.4% (628 patients), raising nosocomial-transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction/expansion and deploy additional temporary isolation structures.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up performance reached 81.6% (challenge table cites 81.3%) versus the 95% target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy, and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Weak alert reporting in some affected health zones risks undetected, silent transmission.
challenges.response: Reinforce community-based surveillance and rapid alert investigation.

challenges.finding: Seventeen Ituri confirmed cases remain not yet ventilated by health zone, leaving gaps in transmission-chain reconstruction.
challenges.response: Conduct data reconciliation, prune duplicates, and reclassify/localize with active field verification.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited training raise nosocomial-infection risk; the challenge table reports 96 health-worker infections and 19 deaths (CFR 19.7%).
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: A backlog of un-analyzed samples in Nord-Kivu and late diagnosis persist amid a 54.2% provincial CFR (challenge table).
challenges.response: Deploy a laboratory catch-up plan and reinforce diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and isolation structures (a gap of about 20 centers) delay transfer and isolation and raise transmission risk.
challenges.response: Urgent deployment of logistics and additional infrastructure.

challenges.finding: Insufficient coordination and weak use of COUSP frameworks cause operational inefficiency and delayed decisions.
challenges.response: Reinforce coordination mechanisms at all levels and operationalize provincial COUSP.

challenges.finding: A financial-resource gap of about USD 20 million limits implementation across all response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and partner advocacy.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations and access to high-risk zones.
challenges.response: Strengthen security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Compromised continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services raises indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effectively implement free care and reinforce continuity of essential health services (CEHS).

challenges.finding: High population mobility raises the risk of rapid geographic expansion; the Wamba/Haut-Uele imported cases stay counted within Nia-Nia (Ituri), and this cycle 2 dead bodies were intercepted at Ituri PoE/PoC.
challenges.response: Reinforce PoE/PoC surveillance and cross-border/inter-provincial coordination.

challenges.finding: Community reluctance toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and community resistance delay confirmation, underestimate cases, and disrupt key activities. Resistance to EDS reported in the health zones of Mandima, Nyakunde and Mambasa, and at AS Soliniama (ZS Bunia).
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of EDS burial teams has paralysed dignified-and-secure burials at Rwampara. An EDS team was attacked while transporting a body from Musenze (Nord-Kivu).
challenges.response: Regularize EDS provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Saturation of isolation structures: CT Bambu 316% and CTE CME Rwampara 157% (Ituri, 15/07); national isolation occupancy is 85.6% (725 patients). Nord-Kivu capacity was not reported on 15/07 (129.6% at 14/07), raising admission delay and nosocomial-transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion and deploy temporary structures.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up is under target (80.3% vs 95%) and heterogeneous (Tshopo 50.0%, Ituri 78.1%), leaving transmission chains uninterrupted. Three Ituri health zones (Bunia, Kambala, Mahagi) transmitted no follow-up report.
challenges.response: Train, deploy, and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and prepositioning at PoCs delay transfer and isolation.
challenges.response: Preposition ambulances (including at PoE/PoC) and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited training drive a high nosocomial-infection risk; frontline personnel carry 119 confirmed cases and 36 deaths (CFR 30.3%).
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) and high mobility raise the risk of urban, riverine, and cross-border diffusion; 151585 travelers passed through PoE/PoC on 15 July and Mahagi confirmed its first case on the Uganda border axis.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC of Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories are still being installed (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo), leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission. A 41-package (363 kg) consignment was delivered to the Mahagi laboratory on 15/07.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralized diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Strengthen security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Compromised continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services raises indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Make free care effective and reinforce essential-services continuity.

highlights: 86 new confirmed cases (Ituri 75, Nord-Kivu 7, Haut-Uele 4) and 29 new deaths (Ituri 25, Nord-Kivu 4); DRC cumulative 2267 confirmed / 893 deaths (CFR 39.4%). New confirmations rose sharply from 56 to 86, the largest single-cycle case count of the outbreak so far, while Ituri's alert-investigation rate continued recovering to 91.0% from 68.9% and 28.1% two cycles ago. The case rise tracks the third consecutive cycle of widening detection capacity, so it measures how much of the outbreak is being seen rather than establishing re-acceleration.

Contact follow-up rose to 83.64% nationally (9886/11820) from 66.9%, but the population under follow-up fell by 1751 in a single cycle with no explanation in the source. The coverage gain is a joint numerator-and-denominator movement and is not read as a transmission improvement. Ituri reached 83.0% (7192/8660) and Nord-Kivu 87.0% (2618/3008); Haut-Uele reports no rate at all, and the province rows sum exactly to the national totals for the first time in several cycles.

No new health zone was affected: the roster holds at 46 touched and 45 actively transmitting, with Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) at day 52 without a confirmed case. Ituri's rise is broad rather than focal, with 13 zones adding cases and Bunia alone adding 25 to reach 606, while Rwampara and Nyankunde recorded deaths without new cases and Logo recorded its first confirmed death. The Uganda-border axis stayed active (Ariwara +2, Aru +1, Mahagi holding at 1), and Haut-Uele added 4 more Wamba cases under an explicit INSP revision footnote.

Ituri's investigation rate continued its recovery to 91.0% from 68.9% and 28.1% two cycles ago, leaving 40 alerts uninvestigated against 121 last cycle. Haut-Uele reported 39 alerts with only 4 investigated, its first alert column after the backfill cycle. SitRep64 does not publish the per-province validated living/deceased split, so those columns are carried as null rather than apportioned from the national total.

challenges.finding: National contact follow-up rose to 83.64% (9886/11820) from 66.9%, but the population under follow-up fell by 1751 in a single cycle without explanation in the source. preserved_conflicts: SitRep64 national headline is DRC-only (2267 confirmed / 893 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 2287 confirmed / 895 deaths / 423 recovered.

The detailed zone table's total row prints 'Nouv. cas' = 56 while the cover KPI, the Table 1 province row totals, the section-1 narrative and the summed per-zone day columns all give +86 (Ituri 75, Nord-Kivu 7, Haut-Uele 4). 56 is the SitRep63 value and is treated as a stale total-row carry-over/typo; +86 is promoted, and it is the value that closes 2181 + 86 = 2267.

The zone table's death subcolumns do not cleanly sum on the total row, while the province table and the section-1 narrative agree on +29 (Ituri 25, Nord-Kivu 4) and the per-zone death deltas sum exactly to 25 and 4 respectively. The province/narrative split is promoted and the total row is not reconciled.

Recovered figures conflict internally and are NOT advanced this cycle. The cover prints 412 cumulative (byte-identical to SitRep63) alongside +32 daily recoveries in Ituri, which cannot both hold; the page-1 narrative separately puts Ituri's cumulative recovered at 406. Per source-review instruction the cover's 412 is promoted as the national cumulative and both the +32 daily and the 406 Ituri narrative figure are preserved unreconciled. Country-scope recovered is therefore also flat at 423. The recovered series should be treated as stalled pending INSP reconciliation, not as evidence that no one recovered.

The national contact denominator fell from 13571 to 11820 (-1751) in one cycle with no explanation in the source, while contacts seen rose from 9079 to 9886. The 66.9% -> 83.64% coverage rise is therefore a joint numerator-and-denominator movement; the source does not distinguish completed follow-up from delisting or reclassification, so no transmission inference is drawn from it. Unlike SitRep63 the province rows sum exactly to the national totals and no rate cluster conflicts.

Tableau 6's isolation split does not close against its own census: 252 confirmed + 460 suspected = 712 against the printed end-of-day 722, a gap of 10. The 722 census is promoted (it is consistent with the 85.9% occupancy over 841 beds and with the province columns 548 + 174 = 722); the split is carried as printed and not forced to sum.

The national bed identity is off by one: 722 (J-1 census) + 119 admissions - 118 exits = 723 against the printed 722 end-of-day census. The printed census is carried, as at SitRep63 where the same identity was off by one in the Nord-Kivu column.

The day's laboratory positives exceed the day's confirmations by one: Ituri 75 positives against +75 confirmed and Haut-Uele 4 against +4 reconcile exactly, but Nord-Kivu records 8 positives against only +7 confirmed cases (75 + 8 + 4 = 87 vs the promoted +86). The +86 case figure is promoted; the extra Nord-Kivu positive is preserved as an unreconciled laboratory-to-case-registration lag.

Haut-Uele's province row (22 confirmed / 13 deaths) is explicitly footnoted by INSP as under revision for harmonization and reclassification. It is carried as printed and its +4 Wamba cases are promoted, but no trend, rate or delta is fitted to Haut-Uele this cycle; its 39 alerts with 4 investigated and its absent contact-follow-up rate inherit the same caution. This follows the SitRep63 backfill cycle, so two consecutive cycles of Haut-Uele figures are provisional.

The cover death footnote is truncated mid-sentence ('Letalite globale 39,4% (893 / 2 267) :.'), so the customary 864 + 29 = 893 arithmetic line is absent. The arithmetic is nonetheless exact and 893/2267 = 39.4% matches the printed CFR, so the headline is promoted without it.

The SitRep64 challenge table is partially carried forward and cites contact-follow-up and CTE-occupancy figures from earlier reporting days that disagree with the SitRep64 operational tables. The tables are promoted for every numeric indicator; the challenge rows are retained only for their qualitative findings and responses.

Tshopo's contact line (76 seen / 152 under follow-up / 50.0%) is byte-identical to SitRep63 and is carried as printed; it is likely a carried-forward row rather than a re-measurement, and Tshopo also drops out of the Tableau-6 occupancy table entirely this cycle rather than being carried at its stale 25.0% rate.

46 health zones are affected but only 45 carry active transmission. Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reached its 52nd consecutive day with no new confirmed case and remains outside the active set in residual surveillance. Both counts are carried and are not interchangeable.

The cover per-province CFR line (Ituri 36.8%, Nord-Kivu 60.7%, Haut-Uele 59.1%, Sud-Kivu 33.3%, Tshopo 80.0%) agrees with Table 1 for all five provinces (745/2023 = 36.8%; 130/214 = 60.7%; 13/22 = 59.1%; 1/3 = 33.3%; 4/5 = 80.0%). challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge; activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of frontline providers (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; return to work announced after the Ituri military governor's intervention) interrupts response activities including dignified and secure burials.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of responders (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; resumption announced after the intervention of Ituri's military governor) interrupts response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise responder payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy 128.4% in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 78.4% in Ituri (556 patients for 709 beds), raising admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance remains weak: Ituri 81.8%, Nord-Kivu 81.9%, both far below the 95% operational target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points cause transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%) drive high nosocomial infection risk, with 121 first-line personnel infected and 36 dead.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) and high mobility raise the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Installation of proximity laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) is incomplete, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilisation and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services is compromised, raising indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of essential-service continuity.

reconciliation.note: SitRep69 prints a full cumulative per-zone table (Tableau 2), transcribed here and verified against the archived PDF. The source states plainly that 'les augmentations importantes observees dans les cumuls resultent principalement de l'integration des bases provinciales harmonisees et ne refletent pas uniquement les nouvelles notifications des dernieres 24 heures'. Confirmed moved 2536 -> 2905 (+369) against only 97 notified in 24h, so +272 is retrospective provincial-database integration; deaths moved 1033 -> 1269 (+236) against 62 notified, so +174 is integration. The harmonization is bidirectional and therefore a genuine reclassification rather than a pure backfill: Butembo 65 -> 62, Ariwara 10 -> 7, Aungba 6 -> 4, Boga 3 -> 1, Drodro 8 -> 6 and Mambasa 8 -> 7 all revise DOWN, while Mongbwalu +118, Nizi +84, Mangala +25, Lita +22, Nia-Nia +22, Tchomia +16, Nyankunde +15, Bunia +15, Rwampara +15, Kilo +12 and Bambu +11 revise UP. challenges.finding: Weak alert reporting, and weak listing and follow-up of contacts around confirmed cases.

Insufficient operationalisation of points of entry and control: functionality remains weak in Tshopo with only 6 of 19 (32%) activated and reporting completeness limited to 57%. Performance is further affected by screening refusals (2,018 people, 2.6%, in Nord-Kivu), assaults on providers, non-observance of the health protocol by some authorities at the Mukulia control point, and a lack of transport for supervision in Tshopo.

Weak IPC implementation: partial decontamination of case households in Ituri (43 of 76 not decontaminated), limited reporting completeness in Nord-Kivu (7 of 11 health zones) and weak score cards (40.9% average in Nord-Kivu, 45.2% at one Tshopo polyclinic), indicating continuing care-associated infection risk.

Insufficient referral capacity (4 ambulances out of service in Ituri, no ambulance in 7 Nord-Kivu health zones and no treatment centre in 4) and saturation of several treatment centres, limiting rapid access to care and isolation of suspects. In Haut-Uele no standard-compliant treatment centre exists across the 6 affected health zones.

Persistent community challenges: an announced strike by the psychosocial pillar and demotivation from non-payment in Nord-Kivu, removal of a positive body by the community to a family cemetery in Katwa, refusal of safe and dignified burials (10 failures at Mangala and 4 at Komanda in Ituri) and refusal of sampling in Tshopo, liable to affect community adherence to the response.

Persistent logistical needs to support the expansion of the response, notably completion of the treatment-centre extensions, continuous supply of essential inputs and PPE, and availability of transport and evacuation means.

Persistent insecurity, incidents involving local authorities and community resistance during safe and dignified burials: physical assaults on providers and on law-enforcement personnel at the Mukulia control point, and insecurity plus a stockout of protective suits blocking 10 burials at Mangala.
Still insufficient coverage of awareness activities and of the prevention, reporting and case-management mechanisms for sexual exploitation and abuse across the zones concerned by the response.

reconciliation.note: Zone rows sum to 5105 confirmed and 2260 deaths; with the 160-death unventilated block that closes on Ituri's printed province row, and the province column closes exactly on the printed national total. Every 24-hour column closes: 84 new cases, 29 community and 13 intra-CTE deaths for 42 total, with 12 unventilated intra-CTE deaths in the residual. Cumulative movement against SitRep 94 is +84 and +42, exactly the printed 24-hour figures. Two zone labels (Boma Mangbetu, Makiso-Kisangani) wrap across lines in the published PDF and their cumulative case counts sit on the wrapped row; both are read positionally and reconciled.
reconciliation.restatement_scope: none; no province is restated and the column closes on the printed 24-hour movement

lab_indicators_24h.note: Per-province denominators only; no national rate is printed and none is derived. Ituri: 52 new positives (27 living, 25 deceased) on 287 new samples, 18.1%, plus 38 repeat positives on a further 90 samples. Nord-Kivu 26 confirmed (3 deceased) on 192 samples, 13.5%. Haut-Uele 6 confirmed (5 living, 1 deceased) with no denominator printed. Bas-Uele's 6 samples and Sud-Kivu's 2 returned negative.

care_continuity: The national isolation/CTE census is 782 patients against 715 across the five provinces that publish a care block (Ituri 470, Nord-Kivu 181, Haut-Uele 49, Sud-Kivu 14, Bas-Uele 1); Tshopo did not report, and the 67-patient shortfall is disclosed rather than allocated.

Haut-Uele publishes a care block for the first time in this run and it is the sharpest capacity signal in it: 49 patients (39 confirmed, 10 suspects) on 78 beds, but confirmed-bed saturation of 400% at Wamba and 216% at Isiro, with only one of seven treatment centres (Watsa) meeting standard.
Nord-Kivu reports 181 patients against 206 beds (87.9% occupancy) with suspect beds at 103.5%, and the Kitatumba and Katwa centres and the Musienene isolation unit all saturated.

Ituri reports 470 patients against 996 beds (47.2% occupancy), with Bambu and Nizi (confirmed) and Fataki, Kilo, Logo, Nia-Nia and Kigonze (suspect) saturated; Wamba recorded six deaths in a single day, which the edition calls a first for the zone.
highlights: The DRC headline is 5105 confirmed cases and 2420 confirmed deaths; the country-scope endpoint is 5125 confirmed and 2422 deaths after the separately sourced Uganda 20/2 anchor.
The edition records 84 new confirmed cases in 24 hours: 52 in Ituri, 26 in Nord-Kivu and 6 in Haut-Uele, with no new affected health zone; the footprint holds at 55 of 151.
Nord-Kivu's 26 new cases are its largest single-day count in this run and take Ituri's share of the day to 61.9%, against 82.9% one edition earlier.

Three of the edition's own headline figures do not follow from the components printed beside them: the national contact rate (84.1% printed, 83.6% computed), the Ituri contact rate (93.0% printed, 86.9% computed) and the transferred-suspect count (105 in prose, 118 in the table).
30 patients were declared recovered, taking the cumulative to 1091 and Ituri's provincial cumulative to exactly 1000.

care_capacity_ituri.note: Ituri only. No national bed inventory is published. The Bambu and Nizi confirmed wards and the Fataki, Kilo, Logo, Nia-Nia and Kigonze suspect wards are saturated. Ituri's cumulative recovered reaches 1000.

challenges: Weak alert escalation and incomplete listing and follow-up of contacts around confirmed cases.

Points of entry under-operationalised in Haut-Uele: 11 of 38 priority entry points activated (28.9%) and 5 of 11 reporting (45.5% completeness), for want of training, supervision and logistic and financial support.

Infection-prevention delivery collapses in Ituri: 7 of 152 expected rings opened (4.6%), attributed to a decontaminators' strike, insufficient teams, insecurity and unfound addresses; PCI reporting completeness limited to 9 of 14 Ituri zones and 7 of 12 in Nord-Kivu, with three Haut-Uele zones (Boma Mangbetu, Gombari, Rungu) transmitting nothing.
Decontamination teams in Butembo, Beni, Katwa and Musienene are claiming unpaid wages for June and July 2026.
Nord-Kivu suspect beds exceed capacity at 103.5%, with the Kitatumba and Katwa treatment centres and the Musienene isolation unit all saturated.
Haut-Uele confirmed beds are catastrophically oversubscribed (Wamba 400%, Isiro 216%), its treatment centres lack water, electricity and sanitation, and only one of seven meets standard.
A body was removed by relatives at Isiro before safe burial, with total refusal to receive investigators, and a Buta body was removed by relatives so no safe burial could be performed.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: The printed national rate of 84.1% does not follow from the printed national counts: 20337/24332 is 83.6%. The five per-province rows sum exactly to both the numerator and the denominator, so the components are internally consistent and the headline rate is not derivable from them.

operational_tables.note: Operational figures are the edition's own printed values. The surveillance text reports 105 suspects transferred to treatment while the alert table's own total column prints 118, and the six province rows sum to 118. The table is carried and the prose figure preserved as the conflict it is. All six provinces report this edition, including Tshopo and Sud-Kivu.

poe_poc_national.coverage_note: Four-province total that restores Sud-Kivu and Haut-Uele and drops Tshopo, which SitRep 94 counted. Haut-Uele's 5780 travellers are printed identically in SitRep 96, so the figure is not an independent daily observation on both days. The basis changes edition to edition; this is not a travel-volume series.

priorities: Reconcile the edition's own contact arithmetic before acting on it: the national rate, the Ituri rate and the transferred-suspect count each disagree with the components printed alongside them.
Relieve Haut-Uele: confirmed-bed occupancy of 400% at Wamba and 216% at Isiro, on a province that published no care block at all one edition earlier, is the sharpest capacity signal in this run.
Restore Ituri ring coverage from 4.6%, and settle the decontamination wage claims in Butembo, Beni, Katwa and Musienene that are driving the strike.

preserved_conflicts: National contact-follow-up rate is not derivable from its own components: the edition prints 84.1% for 20337 seen on 24332 under follow-up, which is 83.6%. The five per-province rows sum exactly to both the numerator and the denominator, so the components agree with each other and only the headline rate is out. The printed rate is promoted and the discrepancy preserved.
Ituri contact rate: the province row prints 93.0% for 13171 seen on 15160 under follow-up, which is 86.9%. The counts are consistent with the national totals; the printed rate is not.
Contact-follow-up threshold: the surveillance text describes 84.1% as 'en -dessus du seuil de 85%'. 84.1% is below 85%.

Suspects transferred: the surveillance text reports 105 transferred to treatment while the alert table prints 118 and its six province rows sum to 118. The table figure is promoted and the prose figure preserved.

Isolation census does not sum: the national headline prints 782 patients against 715 across the five provinces that publish a care block (Ituri 470, Nord-Kivu 181, Haut-Uele 49, Sud-Kivu 14, Bas-Uele 1). Tshopo did not report. The national figure is promoted as printed and the 67-patient shortfall disclosed rather than allocated.
SitRep 95 is DRC-only at 5105 confirmed / 2420 deaths; the country-scope snapshot adds the stable Uganda 20/2/11 anchor separately -> 5125 / 2422 / 1102.

reconciliation.note: Zone rows sum to 5208 confirmed and 2302 deaths; with the 174-death unventilated block that closes on Ituri's printed province row, and the province column closes exactly on the printed national total. Every 24-hour column closes: 103 new cases, 35 community and 21 intra-CTE deaths for 56 total, with 14 unventilated intra-CTE deaths in the residual. Cumulative movement against SitRep 95 is +103 and +56, exactly the printed 24-hour figures. The row count rises 55 to 56 on the Viadana registration, which carries one confirmed case and no deaths.
reconciliation.restatement_scope: none; the footprint grows by the Viadana registration rather than by any restatement of an existing zone

lab_indicators_24h.note: The four reporting provinces publish both a numerator and a denominator this edition, and they sum to the printed national 103 new confirmations on 425 samples: Ituri 82 (53 living, 29 deceased) on 307, 26.7%; Nord-Kivu 12 (7 living, 5 deceased) on 101, 11.9%; Haut-Uele 8 (7 living, 1 deceased) on 15, 53.3%; Bas-Uele 1 (living) on 2, 50.0%. The edition prints no national rate and none is derived, on the same basis as the neighbouring editions.

care_continuity: The national isolation/CTE census of 730 closes exactly on its published parts for the first time in this run: Ituri 447, Nord-Kivu 205, Haut-Uele 53, Tshopo 5 and Sud-Kivu 20 sum to 730.
Nord-Kivu is at 99.5% occupancy, 205 patients against 206 beds, with no headroom left for the next admission.
Haut-Uele expanded capacity to 130 beds by assigning 52 beds at the Wamba and Isiro referral hospitals to treatment centres, taking occupancy from 62.8% down to 40.8%.

Ituri prints only a province aggregate this edition, 447 patients on 965 beds (46.3% occupancy), without the confirmed/suspect split earlier editions carried; two patients escaped the Bambu centre for want of food and 73 patients across six zones receive no food support.
highlights: The DRC headline is 5208 confirmed cases and 2476 confirmed deaths; the country-scope endpoint is 5228 confirmed and 2478 deaths after the separately sourced Uganda 20/2 anchor.
The edition records 103 new confirmed cases in 24 hours, the largest single-day count in this run: 82 in Ituri, 12 in Nord-Kivu, 8 in Haut-Uele and 1 in Bas-Uele.

A new health zone is affected: Viadana (Bas-Uele), taking the footprint to 56 of 151 and Bas-Uele from 1 zone to 2 of 11. Viadana does not adjoin Buta, the province's first affected zone, and lies about 270 km from it; its neighbours are Isiro, Niangara and Rungu in Haut-Uele, two of them already affected, so this is a step across the Haut-Uele frontier rather than growth of a Buta cluster.

The front page reports 35 community deaths while the zone table prints 35 community plus 21 intra-CTE for the same 24 hours, so the day's confirmed-death total is 56 and the front-page figure is the community subset only.
Contact follow-up is 84.0% (18517 of 22043), still below the 85% threshold, and Bas-Uele's own coverage is 18.7%, the weakest in the country in the province that just gained a zone.

new_affected_health_zones.note: Second confirmed case in Bas-Uele province; registered on 2026-08-18.

care_capacity_ituri.note: Ituri only. No national bed inventory is published. This edition prints only the province aggregate, without the confirmed/suspect split earlier editions carried. The Bambu confirmed and suspect wards and the Logo and Kigonze suspect wards are saturated, and 73 patients across six zones receive no food support.

challenges: Weak contact follow-up around confirmed cases, principally in Tshopo and Bas-Uele, attributed to insufficient response teams and community resistance in places.

Points of entry under-operationalised in Haut-Uele: 11 of 38 priority sites activated (28.9%) and 5 of 11 reporting (45.5% completeness); a strike deprived six posts (Dusu, Apodo, Aungba, PK6 Route Niangara, Gossamu, Magambe) of reporting, with input stockouts.

Screening refusals in Nord-Kivu (2383, 2.73%) and Haut-Uele (58, 1%), motivated by denial of the disease, fear of contamination through water and fear of confinement in a treatment centre; some officials do not observe entry-point health requirements.

Infection-prevention delivery short in Ituri: 19 of 74 expected rings opened (25.7%) and 76 of 96 identified sites decontaminated; resistance to safe burial at PK51, Bambu and Mangala and family refusal at Komanda.
Bas-Uele's infection-prevention pillar has no means of transport at all, and faces input shortages and water-supply difficulties.
Very low infection-prevention scores across several Tshopo facilities (11.6% at Clinique William, 12.6% at CS Papa Freddy).

Treatment capacity: Nord-Kivu at 99.5% occupancy with no headroom; Bambu saturated in Ituri with two patients escaping for want of food and 73 patients across six zones receiving no food support; the Buta centre has no water connection and no dedicated ambulance.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: The national figures exclude Bas-Uele: the four counted provinces sum exactly to the 18517 numerator, and to 22041 against a printed denominator of 22043, a two-contact excess. Bas-Uele's coverage (36/191, 18.7%) is published but not counted nationally.

operational_tables.note: Operational figures are the edition's own printed values. All six provinces report this edition and every alert column closes exactly on its printed total. The validated-suspect count of 389 in the surveillance prose closes exactly on the table's 259 living plus 130 deceased.

poe_poc_national.coverage_note: Four-province total on the same basis as SitRep 95, again excluding Tshopo. Haut-Uele's 5780 travellers repeat SitRep 95's figure exactly while its activation rate moves from 28.9% to 36.4%, so the throughput figure is carried rather than freshly observed. This is not a travel-volume series.

priorities: Contain Bas-Uele: a second zone (Viadana) is now affected, contact follow-up there stands at 18.7%, and the pillar has no transport, no water and no dedicated ambulance.
Add Nord-Kivu capacity now: 205 patients on 206 beds leaves no room for the next admission.

Close the Tshopo follow-up gap, which fell to 75.5% from 100% two editions earlier, and raise the province's infection-prevention scores from the 11-13% range recorded at Clinique William and CS Papa Freddy.

preserved_conflicts: 24-hour death split: the front-page highlights state '103 newly confirmed cases including 35 communautaires', naming only the community component, while the zone table prints 35 community plus 21 intra-CTE deaths for the same 24 hours, totalling 56. The zone table closes on every province, so 56 is promoted and the front-page 35 preserved as the community subset it describes.

Contact denominator scope: the printed national 18517/22043 excludes Bas-Uele. The four counted provinces sum exactly to the 18517 numerator but to 22041 against the printed 22043, a two-contact excess. The national figures are promoted as printed and both the scope difference and the excess disclosed.

Points-of-entry throughput for Haut-Uele repeats SitRep 95's 5780 travellers exactly while the province's activation rate moves from 28.9% to 36.4%, so the throughput figure is carried rather than freshly observed on 18 August.
SitRep 96 is DRC-only at 5208 confirmed / 2476 deaths; the country-scope snapshot adds the stable Uganda 20/2/11 anchor separately -> 5228 / 2478 / 1126.

explicit_bdbv_claims: On 27 August 2026 at Kisangani the Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare, Dr Roger Kamba, officially launched Ebola vaccination as part of the response to the 17th epidemic.
The campaign targets health personnel and other frontline responders as its priority group, not the general population.
The declared geographic scope is the provinces of Tshopo, Bas-Uele and Haut-Uele.
The INSP Director General attended as part of the ministerial delegation; INSP restates its coordinating role in the response.
Vaccination is framed as one lever alongside surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement.
normalized_content.narrative_excerpt: First vaccination signal in this outbreak's evidence base. The announcement is a launch ceremony, not a coverage report: it names no vaccine product, no dose count, no denominator and no schedule, so nothing here supports a coverage or protection estimate and none is derived.
normalized_content.publication_title: Riposte contre Ebola : le Gouvernement lance la vaccination des acteurs de premiere ligne a Kisangani
review_notes: PRODUCT UNIDENTIFIED, AND THAT MATTERS. The post says 'vaccination contre la maladie a virus Ebola (MVE)' without naming a product. The WHO AFRO context already archived here (who-afro-outbreak-hub-2026-05-24-live) states that no licensed vaccine exists for Bundibugyo virus disease; the licensed Ebola vaccines are indicated for Zaire ebolavirus. Whether this campaign uses an investigational product, an expanded-access protocol, or a licensed Zaire-ebolavirus vaccine for presumed cross-protection is not stated by the source and is not inferred here. Treat the product, and therefore the expected protection, as an open question.

SCOPE IS THE LOW-BURDEN FRONTIER, NOT THE EPICENTRE. Tshopo, Bas-Uele and Haut-Uele together hold 169 of 5208 confirmed cases on the SitRep 96 zone table (3.2%); Ituri and Nord-Kivu, which are not named, hold 96.7%. This is recorded as printed. Two readings are consistent with the text and the source settles neither: a deliberate westward containment ring around the Viadana/Isiro frontier where the footprint most recently grew, or a phased start in the provinces with the smallest frontline workforce. Do not read the omission of Ituri and Nord-Kivu as evidence that they are excluded from later phases.
